questions.cardText:
[Literature] In which country was the world’s first novel written?
A. India B. Japan C. China
Answer: B. “The Tale of Genji,” written in the early 11th century by Japanese noblewoman Murasaki Shikibu, is often regarded as the world’s first novel.
questions.de: In welchem Land wurde „Die Geschichte vom Prinzen Genji“, oft als erster Roman der Welt bezeichnet, geschrieben?
questions.en: In which country was “The Tale of Genji”, often called the world's first novel, written?

timeline.labelEn: The Tale of Genji by Murasaki Shikibu is complete in its present form by about this year
timeline.labelDe: Murasaki Shikibus „Geschichte vom Prinzen Genji“ liegt spätestens um dieses Jahr in ihrer heutigen Form vor

questions.notes: Card's answer confirmed, but 'the world's first novel' is disputed (Wikipedia: considerable debate; earlier texts have been proposed), so the question asks about the Genji by name. Finished by c. 1021.

questions.cardText:
[Epidemiology] Which of the following is considered the deadliest animal to humans?
A. Mosquito
B. Human
C. Tapeworm
Answer: A. Mosquitoes can transmit diseases like malaria, dengue fever, and Zika virus. Malaria alone accounts for over 500,000 deaths each year, mostly in children under five. Humans come in a close second, causing over 400,000 deaths per year through homicide and war.
questions.de: Welches Tier gilt als das für Menschen tödlichste, weil es durch die Übertragung von Krankheiten wie Malaria und Dengue jährlich über eine Million Menschen tötet?
questions.en: Which animal is considered the deadliest to humans, killing over a million people a year by spreading diseases such as malaria and dengue?

timeline.labelEn: Ronald Ross proves that mosquitoes transmit the malaria parasite
timeline.labelDe: Ronald Ross weist nach, dass Stechmücken den Malariaerreger übertragen

questions.notes: Confirmed: mosquitoes cause over one million deaths a year by spreading disease (Mosquito); malaria alone ~610,000 deaths in 2024 (Malaria), consistent with the card's 'over 500,000'. Timeline from the Malaria page.
